text:
Marathon Petroleum shares fell 0.33% today to $388.38, continuing a sharp two-week decline of 2.77% from their mid-September peak. The broader sell-off appears tied to uncertainty over potential diesel export restrictions — reported today — which refiners warn would ultimately raise fuel prices as they cut production, dampening near-term refining margins. That regulatory concern arrives alongside mixed signals on geopolitical risk: while oil prices rose today on hopes for Iran-U.S. diplomatic talks, the uncertainty itself has kept investors cautious about refiner stocks that thrive on stable, predictable fuel spreads.

Refinery utilization remains solid at 94%, and the wide gap between US crude ($96.41) and global crude ($114.89) typically favors American refiners by letting them buy cheaper domestic oil. However, the policy risk — a diesel export ban would restrict their ability to ship profitable products — has overshadowed that advantage this week.
